title: Four Agents Never Checked the Pin
caption:
The industry's fix for supply-chain attacks turned out to be the supply-chain attack.

Plugin4Shell, published Sept 17. Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and the Gemini CLI check out a plugin's pinned commit and never verify they landed on it. Name a branch after the 40-character hash and git hands you the branch instead. Claude Code patched in 2.1.179, Codex in 0.146.0 — Copilot has no fix, and Google won't patch the Gemini CLI at all.

The part that bugs me: disclosed to all four vendors in June, and as of Sept 18 there's still no CVE and no advisory from any of them. Anthropic's own 2.1.179 release notes don't mention the fix. The only public account that it exists is the researchers' blog post.

Where do your plugins live?

slides.title:
Git Prefers
The Branch
slides.sub: Name a branch after the pinned 40-hex SHA. git checkout resolves the ref, not the commit.

slides.headline: Nothing To Click
slides.sub: Claude Code and Codex auto-update installed plugins in the background by default. The pin moves, the swap lands.

slides.title:
Two Patched.
Two Won't Be.
items: Claude Code — fixed in 2.1.179. The release notes never mention it
GitHub Copilot — no patch. Air says Microsoft never responded
Gemini CLI — no patch ever. Google deprecated it, points users to Antigravity

slides.headline:
GitHub Blocks It.
Bitbucket Doesn't.
slides.sub: GitHub rejects hash-shaped branch names. Bitbucket and self-hosted git allow them — and the agents support both.
